ops.title: codex CLI -c values parse as TOML (raw-string fallback) — free-form strings need JSON/TOML-string encoding; spawnllm >=0.6.2 pins service_tier=fast by default
ops.body:
Two durable facts from the spawnllm 0.6.2 work (2026-07-14):

1. **codex `-c key=value` parses the value as TOML first**, falling back to a raw string only when TOML parsing fails. A free-form string like `true` or `123` coerces to a boolean/int and codex exits with `invalid type: boolean 'true', expected a string`; boundary quotes get trimmed by the fallback. Encode free-form values as TOML basic strings — `json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)` is valid (ensure_ascii=False matters: JSON's surrogate-pair `\ud83d...` escapes are invalid TOML). spawnllm's `CodexCliBackend` does this for `developer_instructions`; controlled vocabularies (`service_tier=fast`, `model_reasoning_effort=xhigh`) are never valid bare TOML, so they ride the string fallback unquoted (codex-ask relies on the same mechanism).

2. **spawnllm >=0.6.2 pins `-c service_tier=fast` by default** (`CodexConfig.service_tier`, `None` drops it). Root cause: `RunSpec.isolated=True` passes `--ignore-user-config`, which silently dropped the user's `~/.codex/config.toml` `service_tier = "fast"` pin — non-fast xhigh runs take 10–30+ min, which presented as "codex hangs via spawnllm but works in a shell" (the shell inherits the config). Note `service_tier=None` does NOT restore the user-level pin while isolated; that needs `isolated=False` too. See [[spawnllm-v040-ecosystem]] and [[uv-exclude-newer-capt-hook]] (the ambient `UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER` also pollutes uv.lock via pre-commit hooks that run uv — commit with `env -u UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER git commit`).
